#prime850club
#patlafriedameats #patlafriedasayseatmymeat #dryagedbeef

When we dry age beef, we’re not just letting time pass, we’re crafting flavor. At around 28 days, the outside starts to dry and darken as water is drawn out, leaving behind a denser, richer beef flavor. That means when you cook it, you’re not steaming it, you’re searing pure steak perfection.

Every cut that comes through our dry age room is precision trimmed, portioned to within half an ounce, and prepared to meet the highest standards in the industry.

This is the largest dry age room in the world, built to create that deep, earthy flavor only time and care can deliver.

Every single night we cut and pack hundreds of thousands of pounds of meat that have to be delivered by morning to a few thousand restaurants. Behind these walls is the largest dry age room in the world supplying some of the most renowned chefs in the country.

Food security is critical because at the end of the week we feed well over a million people. With 52 trucks heading out before sunrise from New York to Boston to D.C., there is no room for error, only precision and trust.

This is what it takes to keep the best kitchens in America running, and it is an honor to be part of that every day.

When you bite into one of the greatest burgers in New York City you’re tasting the work of our incredible team We grind about two hundred thousand pounds of burger meat with complete focus on making sure every blend is perfect A quick thumbs up means we are on track and if not we stop and figure it out right away That’s the level of care behind every bite

I’m taking you inside the largest dry aged beef room in the world, where we’re holding fifteen thousand primals at once. Each cut is carefully aged with no hooks piercing the meat, perfect humidity and wind circulation, and UV lights that protect the beef when the lights go off. The longer we age, the more water is extracted, leaving behind a dense earthy beef flavor and unmatched tenderness. This is where tomahawks, short loins, and so much more develop into the flavors you’ll never forget.

Two cuts, same commitment to the craft.
Ribeye cap pinwheels, rich, marbled, and full of flavor, rolled with precision.
T-bones, the classic steakhouse centerpiece, cut to perfection for a perfect balance of strip and tenderloin.
Different forms, same philosophy: start with the best beef, cut it right, and let quality speak for itself.

After years of R&D and countless tastings, we’ve perfected how Pat LaFrieda meat belongs in Mexico. 🇲🇽

What started as a mission with my good friend Aaron Mizrahi has turned into a movement, bringing our prime, high end steaks to chefs and restaurants across Mexico who’ve never experienced meat like this before.

2025 is our year. This is where we take it to the next level.

I was raised to believe your name is only as good as your product.
.
Every cut we send out has my name on the box, and I take that personally.
.
This isn’t just meat. It’s generational pride, it’s relationships with farmers, chefs, and restaurant families across the country.
.
A hundred years in, and the standard hasn’t changed.

This holiday season, meet Kevin. He’s strong minded, confident, and convinced he’s ready for more. He trains hard, moves fast, and treats every session like the main event…oh and he routinely arrives about 13-27mins after he’s meant to be there. 

John and Seamus don’t mind, right? 

Wrong. John and Seamus see what he doesn’t. The potential is obvious. The structure is missing. Effort isn’t the issue. Direction and discipline are.

One day they decide enough is enough and that Kevin will learn the consequences of his decisions in order to become a better athlete. But a careless wish slips out and suddenly, the gym feels bigger, quieter, and far too accommodating.

At first, it’s perfect. Kevin settles in, takes over the space, and leans fully into doing things his way. The rules fade into the background.

But spoiler alert: the aftermath is less glamorous.

This multi-episode holiday short about ambition, discipline, and why the boring stuff matters is coming soon to a phone screen near you. 🎬🎄

January always feels far away until it suddenly isn’t. Between holidays, travel, and time off, it’s easy to say “I’ll think about it later”… and then January hits and you’re scrambling to figure out where to start.

That’s why we’re inviting you to join now.

From January 5 to January 31, we’re running our January Movement Challenge. The goal is simple: 👉 Move for 30 minutes every day.

Walks, strength training, classes, stretching, yoga, runs; if it’s intentional, it counts. Screenshotting your step count alone won’t cut it here. The point is choosing to move on purpose, even on busy days.

You’ll check in daily through a quick form, get accountability and encouragement inside our WhatsApp group, and build momentum alongside people who are doing this with you. 

This challenge is about consistency, not intensity. Small daily wins. Real follow-through. No pressure to be perfect.

That said… the closer you are to perfect, the more likely you are to win a prize 😉

The challenge is free, open to all levels, and friends and family are welcome. It works best when you’re doing it together.

Joining now means you’re already in the group, already supported, and already in the right mindset before January arrives.

When a new bar or restaurant opens, the internet wants to know all about what they are doing that’s so new and exciting. While that’s all fine and great, anyone with some money can design and open a spot and pay for as much PR and press as they want. We would much rather hear from the New York City institutions that have survived 20 + years in this city. We want to know more about the bars and restaurants that are still delivering on all of their promises. What they are doing to be consistent, to scale up, to maintain standards, to survive the ever-changing neighborhoods and turbulent financial climate of the city. What systems they have tried that failed and what was pivotal to their success. All too often we see places that open to an abundance of fanfare and then they close after 2-4 years. We see menus and service models that make absolutely no sense that unsurprisingly don’t survive past the instagram likes. Real stories from mom and pop and brick and mortar concepts that have grown and survived are in our opinion way more worthy of a conversation. Landlord-owned businesses don’t count. If you don’t have to hustle to pay rent and your business is successful because of the talent that you sought as an attraction, then you’re just holding the keys to the castle (and all the cards).

Big thanks to @aftermath.nyc for hosting and for creating a space where local makers and neighbors can actually connect. As a small, Brooklyn-based, woman-owned business, that kind of community energy really means a lot to us.

While we are not in Ridgewood or Queens shops just yet (always happy to hear suggestions of favorite spots we should reach out to), you can find us at @youghtogo_ in Bushwick, as well as @depanneurnyc and @pecorarolatteria in Williamsburg, and @jubileemarketplace in Greenpoint.

If you tried our chili crisp at the market or have been curious, our award-winning Achilles Heat® Smoked Chili Crisp has layers of umami with a subtle yet bright heat that’s full of flavor. It’s packed with crispy fried garlic and shallots for that full-on crunch, and it’s the kind of thing you keep reaching for and using generously.

Thank you to everyone who came out, supported, and shared the love. This is why we keep doing what we do. 🌶️❤️

Halloween was cutieeeee 👻 

#halloweenparty🎃 #breakfastattiffanys #aftermathnyc #aftermathhalloweenparty

October 31st, 2025: A thrilling night out with drinks & dancing at @aftermath.nyc on All Hallows’ Eve 🧛🏻‍♀️🥂

I really enjoyed putting my vampire costume together using pieces I already had in my closet. I’m always up for a creative challenge! The fangs were the tricky part, but thankfully they stayed on for most of the evening. I kind of freaked my tailor out when I knocked on her glass doors asking to be let in so that I could pick up a dress for my mother before heading out for my own evening plans. “Oh my god, your smile!! And you look like you’ve lost weight!!!” the tailor kept saying as she giggled and handed me the dress. “Thanks,” I said, laughing it off. “I’ve just been running.” She nodded and smiled saying, “Good costume!” 

It was also the first time that I wore three-inch heels in a long time and went out dancing after practically living in my running shoes for most of the year. I didn’t even realize my Garmin kept automatically recording my dancing as a workout til I felt it vibrate on my wrist between each song. Two drinks in was all it took…💃🏻😅 

I had a lot of fun seeing friends and some familiar faces in the neighborhood get all dressed up in spooky costumes as we all laughed, danced, imbibed, and enjoyed the Halloween festivities. 💀👻🎃🕸️✨

Thank you everyone who came to our baby shower showering us with love, support, and baby stuff to help us during our journey as parents. 😊 Although not all friends and family could make it, we appreciate the baby stuff they gifted us. We feel incredibly lucky and loved to have such good friends and family. 🥰 
Yes, Baby Luu is a boy 💙 I am going to be a boy mom! 

Appreciate all my siblings who showed up early to help with decorations. I could not have done this baby shower all by myself without going into full panic mode. Shout out to my sister @jfavro91 for taking care of the games and gift baskets. Making the balloon arch and boba balloon structure were a pain in the butt! Of course I would DIY and not hire professionals to do it. 😅 No regrets! Love my husband @broken_boarder so much for his patience and for calming me down when I get frustrated and anxious over planning the baby shower. Shout out to my sister @wenikii and her bf George for helping us carry all the stuff back to our place and helping us install the tv mount and tv. 

Thank you @wib.nyc for letting us have our baby shower at your beautiful venue. When In Bangkok is one of our favorite restaurant and makes delicious food! Everyone loves the food. Shout out to our server for his patience and organization. He was amazing. 

Thank you @sherocakes for the beautiful boba cake 🧋.

Really good and authentic Thai restaurant near Flushing. The food is on the mid-high end, with classic dishes ranging around $20 each. Really nice and friendly service and beautiful interior. 

📍 When in Bankok (Northern Blvd - Flushing)

🦪 Fresh Oysters ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
- fresh and yummy sauces 😋 it was a bit spicy but i love spicy

🐖 Crispy pork ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
- reallyyyyy good but its a typical pork belly thats lightly coated and fried. I would get it again, its not special but its a classic and cant go wrong. 

🍲 Tom Kah soup ⭐️⭐️⭐️
- my boyfriend really likes it but i dont really like soup soups. It comes with a lot of tender chicken pieces and mushroom. Its is creamy and white from the coconut milk. 

🍽️ BKK Platter ⭐️⭐️⭐️
- I just wanted the chives cakes ( bc its chewy), but the platter comes w dumplings ( the purple/blue thing), and chicken spring rolls as well. Everything but the chives cakes was mid and I wouldnt get it again. 

Other dishes we got but no photos:
🦛 Moo Dang ⭐️⭐️⭐️
- yes the name of the hippo, it was a pork rice platter. Nothing special like moo dang. 

🐓 Chicken Pad Tai ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
- classic and really goodddd. This also came with a lot of tender chicken pieces. 

🫖Thai Iced Tea ⭐️⭐️⭐️
- Really good but too sweet for me.

Found a truly hidden gem located in the heart of flushing called @thesweetsap.Who says there’s no fun in having a solo lunch date, they lied. 

What I Ordered:
⭐️ Mac & Cheese Balls $10 (8/10)
⭐️ Caprese Salad 🥗 $12 (10/10)
⭐️ The Sundance 🍹 $13 (9/10)
⭐️ Fettuccine Carbonara 🍝 $15 + Grilled Chicken $6 (7/10)
⭐️ Cheesecake 🍰 $10 (8/10)

My Experience:
The service was really good. They have a server for outside separate from inside which is great. The Mac & cheese balls could have used some flavor, however the spicy aioli that it comes with bumped it up to an 8. Caprese Salad was fresh all around. The Sundance drink taste like the sweet version of a whiskey sour. Never had snap peas in carbonara before but it was good just needed more flavor. The cheesecake was sooo good especially the toppings were just a perfect addition. Parking was fairly easy.

Found my way to The Trestle in Astoria — and let me just say, it’s giving cozy neighborhood charm with a twist of flavor you don’t see coming! From the moment you walk in, you feel like you’ve stumbled into a local secret — warm lighting, good vibes, and plates that taste like pure comfort.

The standout? Their signature cocktails and creative bites that balance sophistication with that “just what I needed” energy. Perfect for a night out that feels effortless yet elevated.

Astoria never disappoints — and The Trestle definitely added to the list of must-try gems.

We decided to have dinner at The White Radish in Forest Hills. We’d only ever been there for brunch before. Started with a Tomato Bruschetta where the bread was toasted on the grill. Different approach but it worked. The portion was small but enjoyable. Rhea had the Seafood Ceviche- Calamari, Shrimp, & Octopus with onions, cucumbers, tomatoes, & greens. She loved it! Radishes & Burrata- another good dish made with Watermelon Radish, creamy Burrata cheese, Pesto, Cherry Tomatoes, & Olive Oil. I had the White Radish Burger- 50% beef/50% bacon, white cheddar, onion jam, garlic aioli, lettuce, tomato on a brioche bun with fries (fries were very good too) Huge. You cannot open your mouth big enough to fit this burger. Once the juicy goodness soaks the bun you’re out of luck eating it as a sandwich anyway so might as well use a fork & knife from the beginning. Delicious but would’ve liked a little more garlic aioli on it. Both desserts- Tiramisu (what else?) (very strong coffee flavor) and the Orange Cake (tried it because you don’t normally find it in a restaurant) were really good. The Orange Cake had a line of vanilla cream in it. Both were served warm with blueberries, whipped cream, & we’re not positive which- blueberry or raspberry drizzle. We really enjoyed our meal. The menu is small but we’ll go back to try some of the pastas soon. @whiteradishnyc

Casa Enrique is proof that comfort food and fine dining don’t have to live in separate worlds. The menu feels familiar, but every bite has a level of finesse that makes you understand why this spot earned a Michelin star.

The pollo tacos were fresh and bright 😋 Juicy chicken, crisp radish, and a squeeze of lime that tied it all together. Simple on paper, but so well executed it made me rethink how good a “basic” taco can be.
The barbacoa tacos leaned the other way: rich, savory, and deeply flavorful. The meat was fall-apart tender, wrapped in soft tortillas that soaked up just enough of the juices without falling apart. They were the kind of tacos you eat slowly just to make them last longer.😍

Then came the showstopper 🌟: the enchiladas verdes. Enchiladas are one of my all-time favorite dishes, and these immediately landed in my top 3 ever. The verde sauce had the perfect tang and depth, balanced with crema, queso fresco, and a crown of fresh avocado. It was comfort food, but polished. #biteswithrosy

🇲🇽 CHILES EN NOGADA is one of Mexico's most symbolic dishes, born in Puebla in 1821. Legend says the nuns of the Santa Mónica convent created it to honor Agustín de Iturbide, who had just signed Mexico's Act of Independence. They used seasonal ingredients-poblano peppers, walnuts, and pomegranates—to represent the colors of the new Mexican flag: green, white, and red.

More than two centuries later, this dish is still celebrated every late summer when the ingredients are in season, reminding us of Mexico's rich history and culinary artistry.

Roasted Chile Poblano filled with pork, pear, apple, apricot, peach, almond, plantain, and spices.

Topped with Nogada sauce (goat cheese, walnut, dry Sherry wine) and pomegranate seeds.

Served with Mexican rice.

Come and try them while they last.

CASA ENRIQUE - YOU GOTTA HIT THIS SPOT!

Just left Casa Enrique in Long Island City, and I’m still savoring every bite. As a cookbook author and chef, I’m always on the hunt for places where food tells a story. 

Casa Enrique, led by Chef Cosme Aguilar, does just that—his Mexican cuisine, rooted in Chiapas, has held a Michelin star since 2014, a testament to his exceptional skill.

I ordered the Carne Asada, Ceviche de Pescado, and Tostadas de Jaiba. The Carne Asada was grilled to perfection: tender with a smoky char, served with fresh tortillas. The Ceviche de Pescado was a refreshing burst of citrus and seafood, light yet flavorful. The Tostadas de Jaiba, topped with succulent crab, offered a delightful crunch and a taste of the ocean. Each dish was a masterpiece, worthy of its Michelin acclaim.

For dessert, I indulged in two incredible creations. One was a layered pastry with whipped cream and caramel sauce—rich yet balanced. The other was a chocolate delight: smooth, glossy, topped with whipped cream, mint, and a crunchy garnish. Both were stunning and left me inspired for my next book.

The atmosphere at Casa Enrique is warm and inviting, like dining at a friend’s home. I walked in during the day and found a table easily, though it fills up fast. If you’re in Queens, this is a must-visit🔥

Il Toscano, a family owned and operated restaurant since 1985 is a very special restaurant and gem in Douglaston. 

The restaurant is definitely old school, cozy and friendly. All their dishes are prepared with TLC and service is very gracious.  Everything is prepared to order and authentic. 

The zucchini flowers stuffed with ricotta, seared foie gras with cherries, homemade lasagna and napoleon are their signature dishes and all amazing. 

Definitely a keeper and will include in dining repertoire. Highly recommend ❤️❤️❤️
